notes.title: Luminous Skies: Interstellar Update
notes.notes: [p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44256755/efc649840902d1729ed15e45020132df48893984.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Interstellar Update:[/p][p]Added a new planet to explore in the Unknown regions of space. This section of space is uncharted by any faction. The mission starts on the United Commonwealth Home world in a forest on the southern green belt. Prerequisites: Delta 5 Recon Drone must be in the party and the player has completed the main campaign (considering dropping the second requirement but be warned that it was put in place to prevent the player from getting wiped as the missions are rated as harder difficulty).[/p][p][/p][p]Updated Delta's paint scheme to set him apart from the other drones.[/p][p][/p][p]Added new enemy skins. Both the new enemies and their environments are meant to resemble a bleached out environment.**[/p][p][/p][p]Added new armor parts for Delta. This includes Flak Plating and a new Shield, and a Repair Core that are meant to augment machine units.[/p][p][/p][p]For non-machine units, a Flak Armor set has also been added to the game. While this set can be used by any humanoid, it only drops if the player doesn't already have the body armor. Additionally, it is advised to give it to Nori (if the player recruited her), as she doesn't have a unique armor of her own, unlike the other party members. [/p][p][/p][p]If you're unsure, the demo, A Short Adventure, would be a fair gauge if you as a player may or may not want to pick up the full games. [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2384140/Luminous_Skies_A_Short_Adventure/"]It's free[/url]. [/p][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/2384140/discussions/" style="button"]Discussion Board[/url][/p][p]This is more of a hobby for me at this point than something I do full time. That said, it would not be outside the realm of possibility to add more achievements.* One has been added to Horizons/A Short Adventure as a proof of concept.[/p][p]If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to us on the discussion board. There's even a leveling guide there for Luminous Skies: A Short Adventure and Horizons. It's probably the best point of contact. notes.notes:
[img]https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2384221/ss_0db621bd9d81c8a9928102de43bbca416128b95d.1920x1080.jpg?t=1732556650[/img]

Made adjustments for weapon damage types for Luminous Skies: A Short Adventure, Horizons, The Pilgrimage, and Interstellar.

Physical damage now represents blunt force damage. Batons, maces, staves, and fists fall under this category.

Slashing damage covers: swords [wooden ones too], daggers, and axes.

Penetration damage covers: spears, bows, crossbows, and firearms.

The effect of this is less than when an enemy is weak to a specific element. The reasoning for this is that damage dealing characters and their skills were balanced not to have excessive additional damage from vulnerabilities such as these, as opposed to elemental damage.  For example, the Guardian / Vanguard / Defender can one shot a grunt on harder difficulty with a critical hit, especially if the enemy target has been debuffed.

But it does, nonetheless, give some additional texture to the game. Armored targets are vulnerable to penetration damage. Most people and creatures are vulnerable to slashing damage. The rest are vulnerable to blunt physical damage. For example, in Interstellar, switching to a gun will do more damage to robots and switching to a slashing weapon [shiv, chainsaw, and energy dagger] will do more damage to fleshy targets. In Horizons and A Short Adventure, an armored soldier will be vulnerable to a Guardian's Spear and a ragged bandit will be vulnerable to a Guardian's Axe.

notes.notes:
What we have are two new quests, two follow up conversations, seven lore books.

[img]https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/2464111110626597162/D57F67542F22C9800D187EDD41AF5DA8E4EDB782/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img]

A Succulent Meal
Head to the Eastern Outpost and talk the the fishmonger in Tashi Province. Taisa (the werminn Druid) will need to be in the party in order to start this quest.

The Missing Herd
Head to the Western Outpost and talk to the guard at his post in the Snow Drift Outpost. Neve (the werminn Shepherd) will need to be in the party in order to start this quest.

Follow up Conversations
After Completing the quest "Shadows of the Past", return to the tent at the werminn outpost to have an additional conversation with Lina.

After Completing "The Regent's Keep", return to Taisa's burrow and sit down to a well earned meal.

Lore books
More often than not, "show, don't tell" is the better option when it comes to certain mediums, such as video games. But there are times when it may be easier to give people a brief summary rather than spending an overly long time showing people every single detail. This is the case with things such as the lore books that have been added. They give a summary of previous events (albeit, there are parts that are intentionally wrong or missing as these things might have either been intentionally redacted or lost in the passage of time).

There are seven new lore books and one new flyer are available to pick up and read. These are scattered throughout the settlements of the Old World.

New food items are available. Depending on the region that the player is in, there may be a few new items to cook on the menu. In locations such as Tashi Province and Eiji City, fish rolls can be made by combining small fish (raw) and salt. If the player visits Taisa's Burrow with some freshly collected mint plants, she can turn them into a mint chew.

Significantly reduced the forging time for crafting at the Dwarven Kiln in Everstone.

The controls.txt file now contains the leveling guide and where to find party members for Horizons players. So even if the player is offline, there is a guide available.

A few minor fixes were made to Luminous Skies: Interstellar as well.

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to us on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2384140/discussions/]discussion board[/url]. There's even a leveling guide there for Luminous Skies: A Short Adventure and Horizons.

notes.title: Luminous Skies: Horizons Major Update
notes.notes:
We have a major update in store for you this round of patches for Luminous Skies: Horizons [links below].

I'll start with some of the smaller things first:

The difficulty has been increased to several of the enemies on harder difficulties. This was an oversight as these enemies were under powered when compared to some of their counterparts. Some of the larger enemies now have a 20% of wounding their target with a regular attack. We hope that you enjoy the increased challenge.

Added the skill "Energy Strikes" to Nori's skill list.

I've added and updated three accessory items in the game to be character specific. I will elaborate on one that has been in the game for some time [I don't want to tell you about all of them; exploration and finding these things for yourself is part of the fun, after all].

After defeating the Mad Alchemist, the player can return to Oakside and enter into the Temple there. Once inside, there should be a glimmering icon that you can interact with.

[img]https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/2464111110626584986/A019272B5F06C22A33B3F5DDE358F0C51BB8C821/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img]

Once this conversation is finished, a new item will be added and equipped to Anri. It is a personal item, so only he can equip it. 

[img]https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/2464111110626592108/076514AD957944F2118DBE66929AD94954F0AF1D/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img]

This will go for the other similar items that you may find during your adventures.

The next thing is the addition of more weapons, fourteen more to be exact. This was something that had been backlogged my tasks document. Prior to release, one of my testers requested that I add more stats to the gear made available. So I did. For example. the Brigadine armor and Feather Cap [that can be used by anyone], may have lower stats than their heavier counterparts but they have evasion bonuses that quietly make them stronger than they initially appear. Similarly, weapons, like the Dawn Spear, have a chance to inflict vulnerability on a target with a regular attack [a status effect that the both the Guardian and Defender classes cannot otherwise do with this weapon equipped].

notes.title: Luminous Skies: February 2024 updates
notes.notes:
Earlier this year Valve announced they would allow the use A.I. generated content in software published on their platform.

With that in mind, I will NOT be pursuing the use of A.I. in my games. 

At best, the technology is still in its early stages, containing various legal and ethical issues along with it. More importantly, I feel like it would stunt my growth as a developer.

On to the updates:
